metric_definitions.label: Nodes
metric_definitions.definition: Entities in the graph (countries, industries, companies, series, …).
metric_definitions.calculation: Count of current nodes, in total and per type.
metric_definitions.limitations: Counts what RUMIN holds, not the economy: the graph is a small, partly fictional sample and is far from complete.

metric_definitions.label: Edges
metric_definitions.calculation: Count of current edges, in total, per type and per evidence status.
metric_definitions.interpretation: How many recorded relationships connect the entities.
metric_definitions.limitations: An edge records that a source states a relationship; it says nothing about its size or strength, and it is not evidence of causation.

metric_definitions.label: Connected components
metric_definitions.definition: Groups of nodes that can reach each other through edges, direction ignored.
metric_definitions.calculation: Depth-first search from each unvisited node (weakly connected components).
metric_definitions.interpretation: One component means every record is linked to every other by some chain of recorded relationships.
metric_definitions.limitations: Being in one component does not make entities economically integrated; long chains through classifications or currencies are common and uninformative.

metric_definitions.label: Average degree
metric_definitions.definition: The mean number of edges touching a node.
metric_definitions.calculation: 2 x edges / nodes (each edge touches two nodes). Median and maximum are also given.
metric_definitions.interpretation: How densely records are linked on average.
metric_definitions.limitations: Degree reflects how much RUMIN's data says about a node, not its importance. Hubs such as a country or a currency are highly connected by construction.

metric_definitions.label: Density
metric_definitions.definition: The share of possible node pairs that are directly connected.
metric_definitions.calculation: Pairs of nodes joined by at least one edge / (n(n - 1) / 2); edge direction and multiple edges between the same pair are ignored.
metric_definitions.interpretation: Close to 0: sparse. Close to 1: nearly every node is linked to every other.
metric_definitions.limitations: Sparse is normal for real-world graphs; the value says nothing about the economy.

metric_definitions.label: Provenance coverage
metric_definitions.definition: The share of edges with at least one evidence record, and with a citation.
metric_definitions.calculation: Edges with at least one evidence record / all edges; edges whose evidence cites a source / all edges.
metric_definitions.interpretation: Should be 100 % for evidence records: an edge without one is rejected. The citation share shows how many edges point to an external source.
metric_definitions.limitations: A citation shows where a statement came from; it does not mean the statement was verified.

notes: The graph connects the records RUMIN holds. It is not a map of the complete economy.
Every company in the sample network is fictional, and the relationships among the sample entities are illustrative model assumptions.
An edge records that a source states a relationship. It is not evidence of causation, and it says nothing about size or strength.
